title: Ont. man held pellet gun, knives before police shot him: witness
article: Ontario's Special Investigations Unit islooking intothe fatal police shooting of a 24-year-old man that took place outsidehis home on Bonnechere Street North in Renfrew, about 90 kilometres west of Ottawa, around 4:30 p.m. ET on Saturday, said a news release issued Sunday.
The SIU is the civilian agency that investigates cases of serious injury, sexual assault or death involving police.
Neither the SIU nor police would release the victim's identity, but he was named as Michael Foster by his half-brother, Jimmy Leighton, who spoke to the CBC on Monday.
Family, friends and neighbours saidFoster, who was mentally challenged,was well-known andliked in the town.
Leighton said Foster began acting aggressively toward his own girlfriend and his mother on Saturday afternoon after drinking with friends.
Leighton said he wrestled Foster down and their mother called police, hoping that they would hold him until he sobered up.
When Ontario Provincial Police officers arrived, Foster grabbed a toy pellet gun, Leighton said.
"And he was so drunk he couldn't even load it," Leightonadded.
Leighton said police asked him to pick up the gun after Foster dropped it on the ground.
"I'm kind of inching my way because at this point Michael has a couple of kitchen knives, like three in one hand, and can barely hold them," Leighton recalled.
He said his half-brother called again and again for police to come and get him.
Moments later, Leighton said, a police officer fired his gun and Foster was shot in the chest.
"He dropped and that was it," Leighton said.
The SIU's preliminary investigation confirmed that an OPP officer fired his gun and struck the man after police were called to a family dispute at the home.
The victim was transported to Renfrew Victoria Hospital where he was pronounced dead, police said.
The SIU is investigating one subject and four witness officers from the OPP in relation to the shooting.
